headline: Noise, dispersal and nutrient stoichiometry shape ecological equilibria and synchrony
label: Stochastic Population Dynamics Models
summary: Recent preprints apply analytically tractable reductions to stochastic ecological models of synchrony, nutrient limitation and sparse interaction networks.
synthesis: The three preprints, all posted in November 2025, analyze stochastic ecological population models through reductions that yield tractable descriptions of synchronized, equilibrium and stationary states. One uses Gillespie simulations and XY-model theory to show that demographic noise and migration drive spatial synchronization of predator-prey oscillations. A second develops a stage-structured producer-grazer model with carbon and phosphorus co-limitation, parameterized for algae-Daphnia, in which stoichiometric constraints shift equilibria. A third introduces local Fokker-Planck equations with mean-field closure to compute stationary states of generalized Lotka-Volterra models on sparse asymmetric graphs. The common thread is the treatment of stochasticity and structure in population dynamics. What is new is the explicit joint consideration of noise, dispersal, nutrient stoichiometry and network asymmetry as determinants of these states, though the items address these factors in separate model systems rather than within a single framework.
